title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
protagonist: Ishmael (with Ahab as the whaling fortune carrier)

beats.event: Call me Ishmael; he leaves Manhattan seeking a whaling berth
At New Bedford's Spouter-Inn he beds down with the harpooner Queequeg
The two hear Father Mapple preach on Jonah
On Nantucket they sign aboard the whaler Pequod together
Peleg describes Captain Ahab as a grand, ungodly, god-like man
The Pequod sails on Christmas Day; shadowy stowaways glimpsed below
Ahab appears on deck, nails a doubloon to the mast for the whale's spotter
Ahab makes the crew swear vengeance on the white whale Moby Dick
The Pequod hails other whalers, each maimed by Moby Dick
Normal whales are hunted, killed and tried out for oil
Parsee Fedallah foretells Ahab's manner of death
A Pacific typhoon strikes; the compasses are reversed
First day of the chase: Moby Dick bites Ahab's boat in two
Second day: three boats smashed and Fedallah is killed
Third day: Moby Dick stoves the Pequod; Ahab drags to his death by his own line
Ishmael, sole survivor, floats on Queequeg's coffin until the Rachel picks him up
